name: WebLab PWA Suite
author: weblabmd

sections.description:
WebLab PWA Suite turns any WordPress site into a Progressive Web App — installable, offline-capable, and mobile-optimized.

The plugin generates a valid Web App Manifest, registers a Workbox v7 Service Worker, and adds the platform-specific meta tags required for installation on Android, iOS, and desktop browsers.

Why a PWA?

A Progressive Web App provides a native-app-like experience directly from the browser:

  • Installable — users can add your site to their home screen.
  • Fast — assets are cached and served instantly on repeat visits.
  • Offline-capable — the site remains usable without an internet connection.
  • Engaging — push notifications bring users back.
  • No app store — no publishing fees, no review delays.

Install UX (Free)

The plugin includes a complete, professionally-designed install experience with 42 free features that work out-of-the-box:

Smart Banner
* Mobile-only banner (never annoying on desktop)
* Value proposition with 3 configurable bullet points (icon + text)
* Safe-area padding for iPhone notch
* Dark mode support (prefers-color-scheme)
* WCAG 2.1 AA accessible (ARIA, keyboard, focus trap)

Triggers (configurable)
* Time on page (default: 30 seconds)
* Scroll depth (default: 50%)
* Returning visitor (2nd+ visit)
* Exit-intent (desktop, optional)
* Custom trigger via JS API

Dismiss & Persistence
* “Later” button (temporary dismiss)
* “Never” button with 24h-720h cooldown
* localStorage persistence
* Progressive cooldown

Per-Platform Instructions
* iOS Safari: Share → Add to Home Screen → Add
* Android Chrome: menu → Install app → Install
* Desktop: install icon in address bar
* Special message for in-app browsers (FB/IG/TikTok/WhatsApp)

Desktop QR Code
* Scan with phone to install
* Shortcode: [afpwa_qr size=”200″ caption=”Scan me!”]

A/B Testing for Install Messages
* Up to 3 message variants (Free Install UX feature)
* Integrates with the analytics dashboard
* Auto-tracked conversion per variant

Push Opt-in Secondary
* Shown after app install (not before)
* GDPR-friendly
* Customizable title, body, preview

Analytics Dashboard
* Widget in WordPress Dashboard
* Tracks: banner shown, dismissed, installs, CTR
* Per-platform breakdown (iOS/Android/Desktop)
* CSV export

Free Features

  • Web App Manifest — dynamically generated, valid, and cached.
  • Service Worker (Workbox v7) — with configurable cache strategies.
  • Automatic icon generation — all PWA icon sizes (48px–512px) from a single upload (requires GD or Imagick).
  • Legacy icons — favicon and Apple Touch Icons for older devices.
  • Offline page — assign any WordPress page as the offline fallback.
  • iOS support — Apple meta tags and auto-generated splash screens.
  • Android support — Chrome address bar color, Trusted Web Activity hints.
  • Dark mode — separate theme and background colors for dark schemes.
  • Push notifications — via Firebase Cloud Messaging or OneSignal.
  • Background sync — offline form submissions are queued and sent when the connection returns.
  • AMP support — integrates with the official AMP plugin.
  • WP Hide compatibility — works with WP Hide & Security Enhancer.
  • Loading icons library — 4 built-in styles (spinner, dots, pulse, bars).
  • Pull to refresh — native-style refresh gesture in standalone mode.
  • Connectivity notice — customizable online/offline notifications.
  • Scroll progress bar — visual reading progress indicator.
  • Custom 404 page — configurable fallback for offline navigation errors.
  • QR Code Install — desktop-to-mobile handoff via QR code (shortcode [afpwa_qr]).
  • WooCommerce integration — product shortcuts and cache rules.

Premium Add-ons (optional)

Premium features are available through a separate license and an external add-on plugin. The free version is fully functional on its own.

  • Offline Page Builder (drag-and-drop, 10+ templates)
  • Google Analytics 4 integration
  • AI-Powered Caching (predictive prefetch)
  • Real-time analytics dashboard
  • A/B testing
  • PWA to APK (Trusted Web Activity)
  • BuddyPress push notifications
  • White-label branding
  • Priority support

Premium licensing and updates are served from advancedpwa.weblab.md. See the External Services section for details.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • PHP 8.0 or higher
  • HTTPS — required for Service Workers (browsers enforce this)
  • GD or Imagick — for automatic icon generation (optional; WordPress fallback used otherwise)

Third-party libraries

This plugin includes the following third-party library:

  • Workbox by Google — Apache License 2.0. Source: https://github.com/GoogleChrome/workbox

Source code

The unminified source of the bundled Workbox runtime is available upon request or at the upstream repository above.

Development

The plugin is developed on GitHub. Contributions, bug reports, and translations are welcome.

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external services. No data is transmitted unless the corresponding feature and consent are explicitly enabled by the site administrator.

1. License Server — advancedpwa.weblab.md

Purpose: License validation, update delivery, and premium feature activation.

Data transmitted:
* License key (only the license key you entered)
* Site domain
* Anonymous install ID (32-character random string, generated locally on first activation)
* Plugin version
* Device fingerprint — a SHA-256 hash of the browser user agent, platform, language, and timezone

When: Only when the administrator explicitly enables “License Server” consent in Settings → Consent & Privacy. The free version does not connect.

Frequency: On license activation, then re-validated every 12 hours.

Optional: Yes — the free version works fully without this connection.

Terms of Service: https://advancedpwa.weblab.md/terms/
Privacy Policy: https://advancedpwa.weblab.md/privacy/

2. Firebase Cloud Messaging — fcm.googleapis.com

Purpose: Delivery of browser push notifications.

Data transmitted: Subscription endpoint and encryption keys provided by the browser’s Push API.

When: Only when (a) push notifications are enabled by the administrator, (b) “Push Notifications” consent is enabled in Settings, and (c) the visitor explicitly opts in via browser prompt.

Optional: Yes.

Privacy Policy: https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy

3. Google Analytics 4 — googletagmanager.com

Purpose: Site analytics (if enabled).

Data transmitted: Page views and events, as configured by your GA4 property.

When: Only when (a) GA4 is enabled in Premium settings, and (b) “Analytics” consent is enabled in Settings.

Optional: Yes — disabled by default.

Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

4. Plausible Analytics

Purpose: Privacy-friendly analytics without cookies.

Data transmitted: Page views.

When: Only when (a) Plausible is enabled in Analytics settings, and (b) “Analytics” consent is enabled in Settings.

Optional: Yes — disabled by default.

Privacy Policy: https://plausible.io/privacy

5. OneSignal — cdn.onesignal.com

Purpose: Alternative push notification provider.

Data transmitted: Push subscription data.

When: Only when (a) OneSignal is selected as the push provider, and (b) “Push Notifications” consent is enabled in Settings.

Optional: Yes — Firebase is the default.

Privacy Policy: https://onesignal.com/privacy_policy

6. ip-api.com (opt-in, disabled by default)

Purpose: Country lookup for optional geo-blocking.

Data transmitted: The client’s IP address.

When: Only when (a) “External GeoIP lookup” is enabled, and (b) “GeoIP” consent is enabled in Settings. Disabled by default.

Optional: Yes.

Terms of Service / Privacy Policy: https://ip-api.com/docs/legal

Note: This lookup can be configured to run on the license server (WPLMP) or on the client (AFPWA). If neither is enabled, no data is sent.

Privacy

Data stored on your site

The plugin stores the following data in your WordPress database:

  • Analytics events — event name, URL, anonymous IP hash (SHA-256), timestamp. Retained for 90 days.
  • Push subscriptions — endpoint, encryption keys, user agent, subscription date. Retained until unsubscribed.
  • Install statistics — platform and date. Retained indefinitely.
  • Offline form submissions (premium) — form data, IP address, user agent. Retained until manually deleted by the administrator.
  • Real-time visits (premium) — URL, anonymous IP hash. Retained for 7 days.
  • AI access log (premium) — URL and hit count. Retained for 30 days.

Data retention and deletion

  • Analytics data is automatically purged after 90 days.
  • Real-time data is automatically purged after 7 days.
  • AI cache data is automatically purged after 30 days.
  • Administrators can delete all plugin data from PWA Settings → Advanced → Data Management.
  • Full data deletion on uninstall is available via an opt-in setting.

Cookies and tracking

  • No cookies are set by the plugin.
  • No third-party tracking is active by default.
  • Push subscription data is stored in your database only.
  • Analytics data is stored locally (not sent to any third party) unless you enable Plausible or GA4.

GDPR compliance

The plugin provides:

  • Data minimization — only essential fields are stored.
  • IP hashing — client IPs are stored as SHA-256 hashes.
  • Retention limits — automatic purge schedules.
  • Data export — available through the admin panel.
  • Data deletion — available through the admin panel and on uninstall.

Premium license data

When premium features are enabled, the license server receives the license key, domain, and a device fingerprint. The fingerprint is a hash, not personally identifying information. It is used exclusively for license verification.

License

WebLab PWA Suite is free software released under the GPL v2 or later license.

This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the GNU General Public License for more details.

Credits

Developed by WebLab.md.

Bundled third-party library:
* Workbox v7 — Copyright 2018 Google LLC — Apache License 2.0.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the weblab-suite-pwa folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install directly from the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu.
  3. Open PWA Settings in the admin menu.
  4. Upload a 512×512 icon, then click Generate All Sizes.
  5. Configure the offline page URL, theme colors, and other options.
  6. Click Save Settings — the manifest and Service Worker are regenerated automatically.

Multisite

The plugin supports WordPress Multisite. Each site maintains its own manifest, Service Worker, icon set, and settings. A network admin panel is available for overview.

Manual installation

If you prefer manual installation:

  1. Download the plugin ZIP file.
  2. Extract it into /wp-content/plugins/.
  3. Activate it from the Plugins screen.
  4. Configure as described above.
sections.faq:
Why is my PWA not installing?

Check the following:

  • HTTPS is active (browsers require it).
  • The 512×512 icon has been uploaded and generated.
  • The offline page URL is set and points to an existing page.
  • The Service Worker is registered (Chrome DevTools → Application → Service Workers).
  • The manifest is valid (Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest).

The Performance Dashboard inside the plugin performs these checks automatically and reports issues.

Does this plugin work without HTTPS?

No. Browsers block Service Worker registration on HTTP connections. The plugin works on localhost for development.

How do I test the Service Worker?

Open Chrome DevTools (F12) → Application → Service Workers. You can inspect the status, cache storage, and manually update the worker.

Push notifications don’t work on iOS. Why?

iOS Safari supports Web Push starting with iOS 16.4+. The user must first add the site to their Home Screen. Desktop Chrome, Firefox, and Edge support push immediately.

How do I force the Service Worker to update?

Open the plugin’s Dashboard and click Update SW, or save any setting in PWA Settings. The Service Worker version increments automatically, and browsers fetch the new version on the next visit.

Will this plugin slow down my site?

No. The Service Worker operates client-side and does not add any server overhead. Cached assets are served from the browser’s Cache Storage.

Can I customize the offline page?

Yes. Any published WordPress page can be assigned as the offline fallback. The Offline Page Builder (premium) provides a drag-and-drop interface.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes, it works with WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, LiteSpeed Cache, and others. If you encounter issues, exclude /service-worker.js and /manifest.json from page caching rules.

Does the plugin collect any data?

Only what is required for the features you enable. See the Privacy section below.

Can I use the plugin on a client site?

Yes. The GPL license allows you to use and modify the plugin freely on unlimited sites.

Where do I report bugs?

Please use the WordPress.org support forum. For premium support, contact us through the plugin’s admin panel.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

Fix: Implemented proper enforcement for IP Whitelist and Security Headers (HSTS, CSP, Permissions-Policy) via the new AFPWA_Security class.
Fix: Resolved PHP 8.1 deprecation warning (trim null) in the direct file serving interception for manifest.json and service-worker.js.
Enhancement: Improved reliability of the PWA endpoints on servers with restrictive rewrite rules.

1.2.0

Fix: Replaced the custom QR code generator with the industry-standard chillerlan/php-qrcode library to ensure QR codes are 100% scannable by all devices.
Fix: Added direct request interception in AFPWA_File_Server to serve manifest.json and service-worker.js, bypassing rewrite rule issues on certain Apache/Nginx configurations.
Fix: Resolved the activation warning by wrapping global define() calls and dbDelta() in output buffers.
Enhancement: The [afpwa_qr_install] shortcode now auto-detects the /install/ landing page.
Enhancement: Added an admin notice to remind users to create the /install/ page if it does not exist.

1.0.3

  • WP.ORG SUBMISSION: 0 ERRORS on Plugin Check for Free tier
  • NEW: Free/Pro split — hook-based communication via afpwa_load_pro_features
  • NEW: Pro add-on as separate plugin (not distributed on WP.org)
  • COMPLIANCE: Plugin header fully WP.org compliant (Network, Tested up to 7.1, max 5 tags)
  • COMPLIANCE: OneSignal + Firebase SDKs loaded via wp_enqueue_script (was inline <script>)
  • COMPLIANCE: All i18n strings with placeholders have translators: comments
  • COMPLIANCE: Removed .distignore from shipping zip (self-excluded)
  • SECURITY: wp_unslash() on all $_POST / $_SERVER reads
  • SECURITY: sanitize_text_field / map_deep on all remaining inputs
  • SECURITY: esc_html__() in wp_die() calls, wp_kses() on activation errors
  • SECURITY: wp_delete_file() replacing unlink() (10 places)
  • SECURITY: wp_parse_url() replacing parse_url() (5 places)
  • SECURITY: gmdate() replacing date() (2 places)
  • IMPROVED: 4 new phpcs:ignore blocks documenting intentional patterns
  • FIX: Free plugin no longer references Pro classes at bootstrap

1.0.1

  • NEW: Complete Install UX with 42 FREE-tier features
  • NEW: Admin tab “📱 Install” with 7 configuration sections
  • NEW: Mobile-only install banner with value proposition
  • NEW: Per-platform instructions (iOS Safari, Android Chrome, Desktop)
  • NEW: Desktop QR code with [afpwa_qr] shortcode
  • NEW: A/B testing for install messages (3 variants)
  • NEW: Exit-intent trigger (desktop)
  • NEW: Push opt-in secondary modal (GDPR-friendly)
  • NEW: Analytics dashboard widget with CSV export
  • NEW: Auto-generation of all icon sizes on upload (12 standard + 12 legacy)
  • NEW: Physical file writer for hosting without rewrite support
  • FIX: Banner no longer appears on desktop
  • FIX: Removed duplicate install systems (was 2, now 1)
  • FIX: Banner now respects admin settings (was hardcoded)
  • FIX: iOS banner now fully configurable (was hardcoded)
  • FIX: Legacy redirects now work via admin_page_access_denied hook
  • IMPROVED: WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility throughout
  • IMPROVED: Dark mode support
  • IMPROVED: i18n with 1248 translatable strings

1.0.0

  • Initial release
